title: Christ is the Resurrection and the Life
speaker: Pastor Jonathan Landry Cruze

outline.title: The Purpose of Divine Delay
subpoints: Jesus anticipates the outcome with divine omniscience
The illness serves the glory of God
The Son of God is glorified through the resurrection

outline.title: Faith as the Goal of Suffering
subpoints: Jesus expresses gladness at the delay for the disciples' sake
The resurrection deepens and strengthens belief
Faith is a progressive and growing reality

outline.title: The Declaration of Life
subpoints: Martha’s confession of Christ as the Son of God
Jesus as the source of resurrection and eternal life
The promise that believers shall never die

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Jonathan Landry Cruze explores the narrative of Lazarus’s resurrection in John 11, addressing the common human question of why God seems to delay in times of suffering. The central thesis is that waiting on God is never a waste; rather, Jesus often causes believers to wait in order to demonstrate His power and love in ways that would otherwise remain unseen. The text reveals that the ultimate purpose of such delays is the glory of God, as the resurrection of a dead man glorifies the Son more profoundly than the healing of a sick one would.

The sermon further examines how suffering serves to deepen the faith of God’s people. Jesus expresses gladness that He was not present when Lazarus first fell ill, stating that the subsequent resurrection would allow the disciples to believe more fully. This highlights the progressive nature of faith, which grows in depth and content through encounters with God’s power in the midst of tragedy. The passage serves as a reminder that even in the darkest valleys, God is working toward a greater redemption.

Finally, the message centers on the declaration that Christ is the Resurrection and the Life. Through Martha’s confession, the sermon affirms that belief in Jesus guarantees eternal life, transcending physical death. This assurance offers comfort to those facing trials, promising that the rescue and redemption coming through Christ are sure and soon, transforming present pain into future glory.
